I am 51 years old and have farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou County for 35 years. It is just me in the household, so I have learned to save labor wherever I can. My wheat went in last October with a reliable improved variety — something like Shimai or Lumai that has done well on this land before. I rotary tilled before sowing and put down basal compound fertilizer then. Now that spring is here and the wheat is greening up, I will topdress with urea at revival and irrigate three times total: at green-up, jointing, and grain filling. I will spray herbicide early while the wheat is still low, then watch for aphids and spray insecticide or fungicide if they show up. I expect about 960 jin per mu if the weather cooperates.

After wheat harvest in early June, I will plant hybrid maize — Denghai 605 or Nongda 372, the kinds my neighbors and I have trusted for years. I will not till; I will drill straight into the wheat stubble to save diesel and a whole day of work, since I am farming alone. I will apply compound fertilizer in the rows at sowing and topdress with a little urea when the maize is knee-high. Two irrigations from my well are usually enough, one at silking and one at grain filling. Three pesticide sprays total: herbicide at sowing, then insecticide for corn borer. In a normal year I should get about 1,100 jin per mu.
